requirements.quote: `getCourtDay(ctx, {date, scope})` returns items grouped complex -> hall -> list type -> item number, each item carrying proceeding, matter, stage heading (raw and normalised), bench, appearance capacity, assignee, open-obligation count, carry-count and provenance (`source_type`, `anchor_id`, `confidence`, `confirmation_state`). [type:unit]

Scope `mine` returns only items for the calling member's matters and appearances; scope `workspace` returns all items and is rejected for roles without `court_day:view_all` (owner, advocate per owner setting). [type:api]
Items are ordered by item number within a hall list as numeric, not lexicographic (item 9 before item 10); supplementary lists sort after the daily list; ties are broken by serial. [type:unit]

`detectClashes` flags two or more listings on the same date for the same appearing member in different halls or different complexes, and returns both items, the member and the kind (`hall`, `complex`). Same-hall multi-item listings are never a clash. [type:unit]
Clash detection never claims a predicted time overlap; output carries only the factual statement (same date, different hall) so the UI cannot imply a prediction. [type:unit]

`snapshotList` stores an immutable hash and row list of each list ingestion; `diffLists(prev, next)` returns `added`, `removed`, `moved` (hall or item changed) and `stage_changed` entries and is idempotent for identical input. [type:unit]

A diff between a daily list and its later supplementary list is labelled `supplementary` and sorts new rows first; the diff is computed only from lawyer-supplied or forwarded lists (no fetching). [type:unit]
`setCurrentItem` stores the lawyer's manual marker per hall and date with the setter and time; it is an internal note, writes an `audit_event`, and never changes any listing. [type:api]

Exactly one canonical next date per proceeding is preserved: `proposeNextDate` creates a proposal (L2) and, when it disagrees with an existing confirmed date, a conflict card holding both sources; a confirmed date is never overwritten automatically. [type:unit]
A partial unique index `listing(proceeding_id) where canonical` is asserted by a test that attempts two canonical rows and expects a constraint violation. [type:unit]
Matters expected but not listed (a proceeding whose confirmed next date equals D but has no listing) are returned in `expectedNotListed`. [type:unit]
Roles: clerk can read court-day items but strategy-bearing fields (court notes, matter memory snippets) are absent from the clerk payload (column-scoped view). [type:api]
Performance: `getCourtDay` p95 < 150 ms on the seeded chamber dataset (about 40 listings) and issues no more than 6 SQL statements (no N+1). [type:unit]
Sensitive matters (AI-off flag) are still listed but expose no AI-derived fields. [type:unit]
Cross-tenant tests pass: a user in workspace A cannot read or mutate this feature's rows in workspace B via SQL, service, server action or API, including a user who belongs to both. [type:api]
Every new tenant table has `workspace_id uuid not null`, an RLS policy using `app.workspace_id`, and is covered by the CI cross-tenant suite. [type:unit]
Inputs are validated with zod schemas from `packages/validators`; no `any` appears in exported types. [type:unit]
